projects.name: iCANspeed
projects.description: How do systems within cars communicate with each other? This personal project was designed to explore the communication protocols used in modern vehicles and understand their applications. Through this project, I gained insight into the intricacies of automotive communication systems and their role in ensuring seamless operation. Additionally, I applied signal processing techniques to clean and process the communication data so that the data acquisition and analysis could be performed effectively. The setup consists of an Arduino UNO, ESP32, 2x MCP2515 CAN Bus modules, an OLED screen to display speed values, and a analog potentiometer to mimic the gas pedal.

projects.name: PomoRobo
projects.description: Do you ever wish you owned a Pixar Lamp that could help you study? PomoRobo is the next best thing! As part of a group of engineers at HackED 2026, I helped design and test PomoRobo, a modular assistive robotic arm that helps you stay focused and productive. I was tasked with designing the control logic and interfacing the electrical components of the arm. PomoRobo is comprised of an ELEGOO arduino, a stepper motor, a LCD display, and servo motors.
highlights: Built to 3 DOF to reduce complexity and improve usability.

projects.name: Domain Detector
projects.description: Collaborated on an AI model that recognizes the hand-signs from the anime Jujutsu Kaisen. Using a custom-trained TensorFlow model and MediaPipe’s hand-tracking, the system tracks 21 skeletal landmarks in real-time to classify which specific hand sign is being used. This project involved creating a custom neural network from scratch, handling complex dependency management in a Linux environment, and training a lightweight model capable of real-time detection without requiring a dedicated GPU.
highlights: Created a custom process to record hand movements
Reached a 93%+ success rate in identifying the correct gestures in real-time

projects.name: Second Brain TA
projects.description: Worked with a team of 4 to develop a Slack agent that uses Meta's Llama 3.3 70B Instruct model to process student queries, and provide relevant answers. The agent is designed to be a online automated TA that can assist teachers in the classroom, allowing students to ask questions, recieve feedback on their understanding, and help the teacher generate quizzes and lesson plans. The agent is built using Python, Slack API, and implemented with the assitance of Cursor agents.
highlights: Built using Python, Slack API, and Llama 3.3 70B Instruct
Implemented with AI assisted tools including Cursor agents.

projects.name: Splitsies
projects.description: Tired of having to use your calculator to split the cost between friends on a trip? Splitsies is a web service hosted on Render Cloud that allows you and your friends to easily keep track of shared expenses and split costs. The website was built using Python and Flask for the backend, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend. The website is responsive and mobile-friendly, and allows users to create groups, add expenses, and view their balance with friends!
highlights: Hosted on Render Cloud for continous 24/7 operation
Built using Python, Flask, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript

projects.name: Prompty
projects.description: As a team of 4 university students ranging from various programs, we were selected as one of the top 12% applicants to propose a strategic solution aimed to mitigate student career anxiety through the use of a gamified platform that targets the users ability to think critically and make decisions ethically. I was tasked with assisting in the devleopment of the first iteration of the websites's frontend and presenting the final protoype to industry professionals. The website uses generated prompts that asks the user a question and encourages original and imaginative thinking.
highlights: Built for the Digital Innovation Case Competition Competition (DICC) 2026.

projects.name: Ted's Clanker
projects.description: Developed using Discord API, Flask, and a simple Python script, Ted's Clanker is a personal automated Discord bot that tracks user locations and informs members within a server when the user has left or arrived home safely. Once past 10:00 pm and the user has not returned home, Ted's Clanker informs the server and encourages others to check on the user. Using custom API endpoints, Ted's Clanker also allows for timed messages to be sent to the server which can be used as reminders for events or tasks.
highlights: Implemented custom API endpoints for real-time management of users location, reducing manual configuration time by 30%.
Deployed to Render Cloud hosting ensuring 99% uptime and continuous 24/7 operation.

experiences.title: Undergraduate Student Researcher
experiences.subtitle: Faculty of Engineering | Edmonton, AB
experiences.details: Currently researching the magnetophotoluminescence properties of organic-inorganic hybrids in semiconductors. The research project utilizes a variety of instrumentation such as electromagnets, lasers, and spectrometers to study the effects of magnetic fields on the photoluminescence of these materials. The goal of the research is to understand the underlying mechanisms that govern the magnetophotoluminescence properties of these materials and to explore their potential applications in optoelectronic devices.
